title: Halal Explained: From Food Fundamentals to Certiﬁcation
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Mixed audience. Opens with market size and business case, then a Core Principles section that lists what is permitted and prohibited. Cites 1.57 billion Muslims, while the About page says over 1.8 billion.

title: Halal or Not? Decoding Ambiguous Ingredients
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Consumer guide to ingredient names that sound haram or are confused with pork and alcohol (bacon, hamburger, hot dog, and others).

title: Zabihah vs. Halal: Is “Halal” Not Enough?
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Explains the words halal and zabihah and how their use differs in North America. Notes that certification standards differ on slaughter rules.

title: Halal Shopper’s Guide to Ingredients
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Strongest match. Supermarket guide with Haram/Avoid and Investigate Further ingredient lists, E-numbers, and eating-out concerns. Dated 2011.

title: Halal Shopper’s Quick Reference Guide to Products
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Short table of doubtful ingredients by product type (bagel, candy, yogurt). Links a printable PDF. 162 words. Dated 2012.

title: E-Numbers: What Should Muslim Consumers Know?
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Explains E-number food additive codes on European labels for Muslim shoppers. Dated 2009.

title: Is Vinegar Halal?
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Explains how vinegar is made, then concludes that commercially available vinegar is halal. Dated 2008.

title: Does Water Need to Be Halal-Certified?
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Shopper-facing. Explains why processed bottled water can carry certification. Also makes the case for certifying all foods. Dated 2008.

title: Chocolate Liquor, Root Beer, Cooking Wine and Non-Alcoholic Beer—Are they Halal?
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Explains types of alcohol, the 0.1 percent ethanol threshold IFANCA applies, and common misreadings such as chocolate liquor. Dated 2007.

title: Gelatin Traceability: From Slaughterhouse to Capsule
selection_basis: Title reads as consumer guidance. Body read in full in Stage 2.
review_note: Not consumer education. Tells how IFANCA built a traceable halal gelatin supply chain. Better classed as industry and certification. Replacement: Is Kosher Gelatin Halal? (1998), which answers a common shopper question about gelatin on labels.

title: Is Kosher Gelatin Halal?
selection_basis: Replacement for Gelatin Traceability. Body read in Stage 2.
review_note: Explains what gelatin is, its common animal sources, and why a Kosher label does not settle halal status. Dated 1998. Its statement about a named dessert brand may be out of date.
